slab.geometry_and_boundary: one half of a symmetric slab: no-flux center at x=0 and supplied face C(L)=C0; a two-sided slab's total thickness is 2L
slab.limiting_half_thickness: Llimit = sqrt(2 D C0/a) when a > 0
slab.source_relation: One-dimensional steady diffusion with constant consumption, D C'' = a; derived analogue, not a formula attributed to Grimes et al.

sphere.geometry_and_boundary: spherical domain with supplied outer boundary C(R)=C0 and symmetry at the center
sphere.limiting_radius: Rlimit = sqrt(6 D C0/a) when a > 0
sphere.source_relation: Grimes et al. 2014, Eq. 2.2 spherical Laplacian and Eq. 2.6 diffusion-limit radius; written in partial-pressure form as r_l = sqrt(6 D p0/(a Omega)).

common_assumptions: diffusion only; no perfusion or advection
spatially constant, nonnegative oxygen consumption a
oxygen profile is evaluated only within the stated ideal geometry
model.derived_output: model-predicted center oxygen content Ccenter; Ccenter < 0 marks that the nonnegative-oxygen profile is outside this constant-consumption model's domain, not a physical negative concentration
model.units_note: The existing lifecycle profiles use the same mass basis as the cited Grimes source: C0 is oxygen-gas volume per tissue mass and a is that volume consumed per tissue mass per second. C0/a is seconds. If a downstream context uses per-volume values, both must be converted consistently; this artifact does not do that conversion.

Omega.status: source-context conversion, recheck temperature/material before use

a.meaning: oxygen consumption per tissue mass per time

p0.unit: mmHg when using the Grimes pressure conversion

not_established: cell viability threshold or tissue survival
cell-specific oxygen consumption or diffusion in either candidate project
actual oxygen supply in a microcarrier or repair patch
wound closure, epithelial barrier function, microcarrier motion or organism-level function
a transfer relation from tumor spheroids, fish, Xenobots, or another cell/material context
